title: Bangladesh Opener Shadman Islam Ruled Out of South Africa Tour With Ankle Injury
excerpt: Shadman Islam twisted his left ankle fielding in the Sylhet Test against West Indies, leaving Bangladesh a batter short; team medical staff suspect a hairline fracture and ligament damage that could sideline him for three to four weeks.
body:
• Bangladesh Test opener Shadman Islam, 31, has been ruled out of the South Africa tour after twisting his left ankle while fielding on day two of the second Test against West Indies in Sylhet.
  • The BCB medical department suspects a hairline fracture plus ligament damage and estimates three to four weeks to return to play, pending the full MRI report.
  • Shadman could not bat in Bangladesh's first innings in Sylhet — the team batted one short — a week after his 105 in the first Test at Mirpur, his third Test century.
  • In-form opener Mahfizul Islam Robin, already training with the squad in Sylhet, is reported to be in line to replace him in the Test squad; the tour opens with the first Test in Johannesburg on November 15.

Bangladesh will tour South Africa without the opener who has been holding their top order together. Shadman Islam has been ruled out of the tour after twisting his left ankle while fielding in the second Test against West Indies in Sylhet, the Bangladesh Cricket Board's medical staff confirmed, with a suspected hairline fracture and ligament damage.

How the injury happened

The injury came on day two in Sylhet, in the 78th over of West Indies' first innings. Shadman chased a ball that Amir Jangoo had flicked towards fine leg off Mehidy Hasan Miraz, slipped as he went to collect it, and his left ankle caught in the grass and twisted. His shoe was removed on the field, he was carried off on a stretcher and taken to hospital in a wheelchair for an MRI scan, with the ankle swollen.

"Shadman hurt his left ankle today. So he couldn't field anymore. We have kept him under observation. He was also scanned," team physio Bayjedul Islam said. "However, at the moment he is not in a condition to bat in the first innings." Bangladesh batted one man short in that innings. The BCB medical department later said: "An MRI was conducted that same day. The report has not yet arrived, but based on an initial assessment, we suspect there might be a hairline fracture in the bone. There is also an issue with the ligaments. In that case, it could take 3-4 weeks to become fit for play." A member of the selection panel told Cricbuzz: "He is ruled out from the South Africa tour. As far as my knowledge is concerned, he suffered a tear while there is a possibility of a fracture as well." The exact diagnosis awaits the full scan report, and no recovery timeline has been formally confirmed.

"He was also scanned," team physio Bayjedul Islam said."

What Bangladesh lose

The timing is cruel. In the first Test of this series, at Mirpur, Shadman scored 105 off 234 balls — his third Test century — to give Bangladesh a first-innings lead. Across 33 Tests he has 1,696 runs at an average of 29.24, numbers that understate his current value: he is the settled half of Bangladesh's opening pair, and the South Africa tour — two Tests in the World Test Championship, starting at the Wanderers on November 15 and SuperSport Park on November 23, followed by three ODIs and three T20Is — is the hardest opening assignment in the game.

Cricbuzz and IANS both report that Mahfizul Islam Robin, an in-form opener from Mymensingh, is in line to take Shadman's place in the Test squad. Robin is already in Sylhet training in the nets with the national coaches, though his selection has not been formally confirmed. Bangladesh's tour squads had not been published when the injury news broke — which is why a replacement can still be absorbed without a formal withdrawal. What cannot be absorbed so easily is the loss of a century-maker in form, a week before facing Kagiso Rabada and Anrich Nortje at the Wanderers.
nri_angle: Bangladesh's full-format South Africa tour is a marquee series for South Asian cricket fans in the diaspora, and the visitors have lost their in-form Test opener before it starts.
